summary: The bracket cannot be made with 3-axis milling and the Ø6 minimum tool as modelled: Pocket1 has 4 sharp internal vertical corners, the Ø3 x 36 blind pin hole is 12xD deep, and the part needs 4 setup directions; wall and floor thicknesses are fine.

flags.title: Pocket1 has sharp internal vertical corners that cannot be milled
flags.evidence: The snapshot reports 4 sharp internal edges, all on Pocket1's 4 vertical corners (parts[0].sharp_internal_edges = 4). CON-003 is 3-axis CNC milling with a minimum tool of Ø6, so these corners need at least R3. Pocket1 dimensions are D1 = 30 mm and D2 = 6 mm. D2 = 6 is most likely the depth, which matches the 4.0 mm minimum wall (10 mm base minus 6 mm).
flags.recommendation: Round the 4 vertical corners of Pocket1 to R4. That is slightly more than the R3 radius of a Ø6 end mill, so the cutter does not wrap the corner fully and chatter. R3 is the absolute minimum. The other option is to open the pocket into a through-slot.

suggested_change.detail: Fillet R4 (at least R3) on the 4 vertical internal edges of Pocket1

flags.title: Pin hole is 12 times its diameter deep and blind
flags.evidence: The pin hole is Ø3.0 x 36.0 mm, blind, drilled along +x from the x = 0 face at [0, 30, 25] (holes[1]; D1@Pin hole = 3, D2@Pin hole = 36). Depth over diameter is 36 / 3 = 12, above the critical limit of 10. The blueprint does not accept gun drilling. No requirement explains why the hole has to be this deep.
flags.recommendation: Make the hole no deeper than 18 mm (6xD) at Ø3, or enlarge it (Ø6 allows 36 mm at 6xD), or make it a through-hole from the nearest face. If the depth really is needed, the engineer has to accept a long-series drill with peck drilling and add that acceptance to the blueprint.

suggested_change.detail: Pick one: D2@Pin hole set to 18 mm or less, Ø raised to 6 mm or more, or a spec_change accepting deep drilling for the pin hole

flags.title: 4 setup directions on a 3-axis process
flags.evidence: The snapshot lists 4 setup directions (+z, -z, -x, +y) against a limit of 3 for 3-axis work (CON-003). +z covers the pocket and counterbores, -z is the back face (datum A, INT-001), and -x is only for the pin hole. What needs +y is not identified; there are 2 faces with normal +y totalling 1650 mm².
flags.recommendation: Cut the setups to 3 or fewer. Find which feature needs +y and move it so it can be reached from +z or -x. Alternatively, drill the pin hole from +z, or leave the -z face as the stock face so it needs no machining.

suggested_change.detail: Remove the +y setup, or merge -x into a 4th-axis/vise rotation, so there are 3 or fewer setup directions

flags.title: Fillet1 R2 is below the R3 radius of the minimum tool
flags.evidence: Fillet1 has 2 internal radii of R2.0 (internal_radii_mm). CON-003 sets the minimum tool at Ø6, which gives R3. If these edges are vertical, a Ø6 end mill cannot produce them. If they are floor-to-wall edges (the Base/Upright junction), they need a Ø6 bull-nose cutter with an R2 corner. The snapshot does not give the edge orientation.
flags.recommendation: Raise Fillet1 to R3 or more (R4 is better for vertical edges). If these are floor-to-wall edges and R2 is needed for strength, say in the blueprint that a corner-radius cutter is required.

suggested_change.detail: Fillet1 radius from 2 mm to 3 mm or more
